shop._v110_note: v1.10 (QA review_r3_01ac_v19). (c) live limitation: in the live market other shops' orders/results keep coming, so the v1.9 market reference (demand_ref) never goes stale and the idle pause is effectively OFF in live; the binding inventory bound in live is (a) max_inventory_cost_frac. idle_ref_scope 'own': while our sellable stock is above low_stock, restock pauses when OUR shop had no demand evidence (own settle matched by owner.own_shop_keys: norm_name over own_shop_names + cached/R3_SHOP_NAME names, our shop URL or <market>/shop/<name>, pubkey; a buyer asking us for stock we lack = seller no_stock in metrics.jsonl; manual resume) for idle_pause_s (before the first own sale: since our first stock). At or below low_stock the v1.9 market rule decides (a sold-out shop has no own settles). idle_low_stock_frac 0.25: low_stock also when sellable cost <= 0.25 x the (a) cap, so one unsellable unit no longer deadlocks the no-signal branch. Resume-file mtime is clamped to now (a future mtime counts as 'now' once, then ages). Decision evidence (tools/sim_idle_scope.py, 72 h real-time, other shops' orders always fresh, tuning catalogs seeds 7/11/212, mock/sim_v110/): own vs market: no own demand S1 cash +35,760..+68,160 (2-3 buys vs 4), demand stops after 24 h S3 0..+73,320, steady/on-off/half-category demand S2/S4/S5 identical (no lost sales); frac 0 vs 0.25 identical in all scenarios (the deadlock case is a unit test). Kept 'own' + 0.25. It does not stop the 1-2 refills right after demand ends (6 h window); the (a) cap bounds that. R3_IDLE_REF_SCOPE overrides (mock A/B only).
shop._v111_note: v1.11 (QA review_r3_01ac_v110). Own demand also = our seller hook's accept rows in metrics.jsonl (restock.market_activity own_accepts / last_own_accept_ts, policy.own_demand_ref 'own_accept'): independent of the ledger settle shop format and of the own_shops.json tunnel-URL cache, so a changed tunnel URL or an unmatched settle shop field no longer starves the own gate while buyers buy from us; first_stock counts only before any own settle or accept. <market>/shop/<name> is percent-decoded (LSS%20Shop). Monitor (v1.12 rule; this sentence corrected in v1.14, it described the v1.11 rule): ACT when our own ledger settles >= 3 but our seller accepts = 0, i.e. the accept signal is broken (revert idle_ref_scope=market in the first hour after deploy: labpc_swap_checklist 3-0); WATCH partial accept loss when accepts >= 1 and own settles >= accepts + 3; the own-gap line is ACT only above low_stock (WATCH 'does NOT pause' at or below it); WATCH at >= 80% of the (a) cap. (a) max_inventory_cost_frac 0.12 x balance (about 550k-600k won at a 4.6M-5M balance) is the real end-inventory risk ceiling: when demand ends the shop is sold out (low_stock), the market rule refills up to (a) (1-2 refills after the first stock), and only then the own 6 h window starts (QA 211 real ratio: 533,484 = 96% of 553,902). No change to the decision (own, frac 0.25).
shop._v19_note: v1.9 (QA review_r3_01ac_v17). (c) deadlock fix: the idle reference is the newest market demand evidence (policy.demand_ref): market order/result rows of any buyer (GET /api/ledger, kept in the ledger cursor), market settles of any shop, or a manual resume (touch <R3_STATE>/restock_resume). Orders keep coming while buyers exist, with or without our stock, so a sold-out shop keeps restocking while there is demand and pauses only when the whole market is quiet for idle_pause_s. With no order/result seen at all (no R3_MARKET, cursor lost) the v1.7 settle/first-stock reference is used, and the gate does not pause at idle_low_stock_units (0 = sold out) or fewer sellable units. (b) velocity_include_own: restock_plan adds our own shop's sales rate (decayed settle count by SKU, own_velocity_tau_h, aggregates' estimator; aggregates' velocity_per_h excludes our shop) to the category velocity for ranking and the food cap: our sales are demand too. Tuned on 7, 11 (40) and 212 (120, 600 orders) (mock/RUNS.md v1.9): include_own on/off and idle_low_stock_units 0/2; same settled and gpc, cash within run-to-run spread; kept on and 0.

(c) idle_pause_s: no market settle (any shop) for this long since the last settle (before the first settle: since our first stock) -> restock pauses, in v1.7 also when sold out [v1.9 correction: the v1.7 text said holding stock; v1.7 code paused sold-out shops too, see _v19_note] (R3_IDLE_PAUSE_S overrides, mock only). restock_stop_before_end_h: no restock in the last hours of the round. Tuned 11/3 on seeds 7, 11 (40 orders) and 212 (120 orders) only, mock storage off and on (--storage-scale 1440), round window pinned: frac 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05 vs none; only 0.01 changed a decision (212: second restock 55 -> 54 units, -11,444 cost; gpc net of storage +502 with the fee, equal without; 7/11 unchanged). Held-out on fresh seeds: mock/RUNS.md v1.13. The cap is a risk bound, not break-even (margin ~25-45 % of cost = 25-45 days of fee). accept_c._note: v1.4 (G): a shop that states grade C (or claims C on the receipt) is no longer walked away from: we haggle on with cap = min(cap, list x max_pay_frac) and pass accept.grades + C for that deal only. taste._note: v1.19: restock ranks categories by the taste forecast (buyer trajectories in the memory graph, taste/forecast.py) only while <R3_STATE>/taste_gate.json says "adopted" and its asof is at most max_age_s old. The gate (taste/gate.py, prereg taste-v1, pinned judge taste/judge.py) adopts when the 1-0.05/6 hour-bootstrap CI of mean d = L_B - L_A (log loss of next-hour settles by category, velocity ranking B vs taste A) is above 0 at 6/12/24/48/96/192 evaluable hours, and rolls back when mean d over the last 24 evaluable hours < 0. Only the category order changes; targets, caps, budget, window gate and below-market filter do not. enabled false = velocity ranking regardless of the gate.
